headline: Your liver cannot hear GH
punch: This is why the same dose gives different numbers.

headline: We left a question open
body: So in the IGF-1 ceiling post we saw that the same GH dose produced IGF-1 all over the range, with the dose ranges for the high and low IGF-1 groups overlapping almost completely at 0.01 to 0.10 mg/kg/day. | That spread has a mechanism and it is not genetics or luck or measurement error. It is how much insulin your liver is being exposed to, and once you know that, several other odd findings in this series line up behind it.

headline: What does insulin do at the liver?
body: Portal insulin, meaning the insulin arriving at your liver directly from the gut before it reaches the rest of you, **stimulates hepatic GH-receptor protein synthesis and its translocation to the cell surface**. | So insulin is not a bystander in this axis. It determines how many GH receptors your liver puts out on its surface to catch the signal with in the first place, which makes it upstream of everything GH does hepatically.
punch: _No receptors on the surface, no response to GH._

headline: The plain version
body: Without adequate portal insulin exposure, **the liver cannot fully respond to GH**. | You can inject as much growth hormone as you like. If the receptor density on those cells is down, the signal arrives and nothing catches it. It is a radio with the antenna disconnected, and the amount of broadcasting you do is not the limiting variable.

headline: The cleanest test
body: Take 17 adults with type 1 diabetes off their basal insulin for **8 hours** and watch what happens to the IGF-1 system. This is the experiment you cannot ethically design, so it is valuable that the condition provides it. | *IGFBP-1*, the binding protein that takes IGF-1 out of circulation, rose from **32 to 205 ng/mL**, a 6.4-fold increase. Total IGF-1 fell 19%. And free IGF-1 fell **below the detection limit in 15 of the 17 patients**.
punch: Eight hours without insulin. Free IGF-1 gone.

headline: Then they gave it back
body: A single dose of insulin, 0.2 units per kilogram. Two hours after that, free IGF-1 had **rebounded to 0.54 ng/mL** from undetectable, against a baseline of 0.72. | So this is not a slow adaptation over weeks of poor control. The hepatic IGF-1 system tracks insulin on a timescale of hours, in both directions, and it does it fast enough that when you measure matters as much as what you measure.

headline: Is this just blood sugar control?
body: This is the part that surprised me most. Switching patients from subcutaneous insulin to **continuous intraperitoneal** delivery, which sends insulin to the liver first the way the pancreas does, dropped IGFBP-1 by **100.7 µg/L**, p < 0.01. | And there was no meaningful relationship between the change in HbA1c and the change in IGFBP-1, r = -0.3, p = 0.33. The delivery route mattered. The quality of glucose control did not.
punch: ==Where the insulin lands beats how well it controls glucose.==

headline: They tested that again
body: Four different insulin preparations given at an identical dose produced **parallel decreases in IGFBP-1 despite marked differences in peripheral insulin concentration and plasma glucose**. | The authors' conclusion was blunt and worth quoting: glycemic response cannot predict IGF-system response. Two different systems reading the same hormone and reporting completely different things about it.
punch: Your glucose number does not tell you this.

headline: Which explains something odd
body: Obese subjects respond to injected GH with **higher IGF-1 rises than lean subjects**, and Cushing's syndrome shows a supranormal IGF-1 response to the same GH. Both of those look backwards until you know the mechanism. | Both are states of elevated hepatic insulin exposure. More insulin at the liver means more GH receptor on the surface means more IGF-1 out of the identical dose of growth hormone.
punch: More hepatic insulin, bigger IGF-1 response.

headline: It shows in the route of a pill
body: Oral estradiol raised IGFBP-1 by **170%** and lowered IGF-1 by **43%** in patients on GH treatment. Transdermal estradiol did **neither**. | Same hormone, same patients, same dose. The preparation that passes through the liver first on its way into circulation rewired the entire axis. The one that skipped first-pass metabolism left it untouched. Route is not a detail here, it is the variable.

headline: What this means
body: Your serum IGF-1 is simultaneously reporting on your GH dose, your hepatic insulin exposure, the route anything you take reaches the liver by, your body composition, and your pubertal stage. | It is a composite of at least five inputs. Treating it as a dial that only your GH dose moves is reading one of those five and attributing the whole reading to it.
punch: ==IGF-1 is a composite, not a GH readout.==
